name: 2101 Prairie Avenue — brick corner house of two and a half storeys on 21st Street, K01 frontage assembly

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body on its 21st Street side (this frame's v 0), read off sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn at full size (T-3665) and carried into this frame through the committed fit of the trace (data/traces/prairie_1904_footprints_s35.json, 0.1858 m a pixel): the main rear wall at column 1034 and the 21st Street wall at row 1000.5. The sheet's georeference carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of reading on this copy. The draft's corner stood about 0.06 m east and 0.17 m south of this one, its rectangle fit stopping short of the walls. Rotation 179.38 degrees (the draft's) turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 2101 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_2101 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).

footprint.note: The main body: 21.93 m from the rear wall (column 1034) to the front (column 916), and 11.15 m along the front from the 21st Street wall (row 1000.5) to the south wall (row 1060.5), read off sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn at full size (T-3665) and carried into this frame through the committed fit of the trace (data/traces/prairie_1904_footprints_s35.json, 0.1858 m a pixel). The draft's fit drew it 20.5 by 9.75 m. The sheet sets the front's north end back about 1.5 m for 3.25 m (column 924, to row 1018), a recess its one-storey frame porch fills; K01 lays the main block as a rectangle, so the front stands in its main line there.

stories.note: '2½B' printed on the 1911 sheet: two full storeys and a half storey in the roof, the attic lit by a dormer (form.dormer).

construction.note: The sheet colours the house pink, brick, with no stone band across its front (2001's and 2109's fronts carry the blue one).

bays.note: The sheet's frame (yellow) additions to the house, read off sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn at full size (T-3665) and carried into this frame through the committed fit of the trace (data/traces/prairie_1904_footprints_s35.json, 0.1858 m a pixel): two canted one-storey bays on the 21st Street flank, reaching the street line 0.95 m out (columns 931.7-955 and 968-992.5: u 14.7-19.0 and 7.7-12.3), and a two-storey frame projection ('2') on the south flank, 1.3 m out (columns 941-965, rows 1060-1067.5: 4.84-9.32 m from the front; built 1.2 m out, the most K08 stands a projection proud). Their places and storeys are the map's; their heights, faces, lights and low hipped tops are K08's reconstruction.

window_kit.note: RECONSTRUCTED: K06 two-over-two double-hung sash in every wall; the basement lights the kit's area light. The kit's commonest forms, not a reading of this house (liberty L-k01-2101-corner-3665).

entrance_kit.note: RECONSTRUCTED: a panelled door on a stone stoop; the front yard 7.25 m deep to the front lot line (column 877) (liberty L-k01-2101-corner-3665).

boundary.note: RECONSTRUCTED: no boundary across the front: no picture of this front is held; the lot's sides are the 21st Street line (row 995) and the line with 2109 (row 1120) in this frame (liberty L-k01-2101-corner-3665).

yard.note: RECONSTRUCTED: a flagged front walk to the stoop over an earth front, 2001's (liberty L-k01-2101-corner-3665).

street_front_trim.note: RECONSTRUCTED: stone lintels under cornice hoods over the principal storey's lights and plain flat lintels under the cornice over the chamber storey's, 2003's brick front (liberty L-k01-2101-corner-3665).

rear_wings.note: The sheet's attached rear range (census s35-2101-wing, 'a long rear range reaching back toward the alley'), read off sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn at full size (T-3665) and carried into this frame through the committed fit of the trace (data/traces/prairie_1904_footprints_s35.json, 0.1858 m a pixel): 4.65 m out from the main rear wall (column 1034 to 1059.5) and from row 1032 to row 1078.5 (v 5.85-14.5), standing 3.35 m out past the main body's south wall. Its place and brick are the map's; its two storeys on the main body's floors, sash, lights and flat painted-tin deck are K01's reconstruction. The small one-storey frame piece on its rear (columns 1059.5-1065) is not built.

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '2½B brick dwelling (D) on the 21st Street corner, with one-storey frame porches' (census row s35-2101-front). Carried to 1904 on the T-1842 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 35.
what_it_supplies: Footprints, lots and street widths from 20th to 22nd Street between Indiana and Calumet, as of 1911, at the copy's coarser resolution
The position of Twentieth Street, which is vacated between Indiana and Calumet today
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
Any lake edge: the sheet ends at Calumet Avenue

research_note: T-3665 (piece 1 of T-1924, the S13 package of the T-1837 programme) refines the district draft (T-2352) in place under the same id: the house is rebuilt from the K01 frontage assembly and its kits — K03 brick walls, K06 sash, K07 door and stoop, K08 frame bays and a frame projection, K10 bracketed cornice, a K04/K05 hip with a K05 dormer and the attached rear range — instead of the draft builder. What is read: sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn at full size (storeys '2½B', brick, 'D', the main body 21.9 by 11.15 m on the 21st Street line, the long rear range stepping out past the south wall, two one-storey frame bays on the 21st Street flank and a two-storey frame projection on the south flank) through the T-1842 census, which rules it present in 1904. No photograph, plate or description of the house is known (the Prairie library holds none under 2101), so every height, opening, roof and detail is the kits' reconstruction under liberty L-k01-2101-corner-3665. The sheet's one-storey frame porches across the front and round its south-west corner are not built: K01 lays no frame porch on a street front. Review: docs/RESEARCH/k01-2101-corner-3665/README.md.
